meta.description: This program allows bank staff to view the full details of a credit card account by entering an account number, retrieving and displaying associated account and customer information on screen.
meta.process_description: A bank staff member enters a credit card account number on the Account View screen. The program validates the input (ensuring it is numeric, non-zero, and 11 digits), then looks up the account in the card cross-reference file, retrieves the full account record from the account master file, and retrieves the associated customer record from the customer master file. The combined account and customer details are then displayed on screen for the staff member to review. From this view screen, the staff member can navigate to related functions such as the card list, card detail, card update, or return to the main menu.

files.ACCTDAT: Account master file containing credit card account details such as credit limit, balance, and status
files.CUSTDAT: Customer master file containing personal and contact details of the account holder
files.CARDDAT: Card master file containing individual credit card records linked to accounts
files.CARDAIX: Alternate index on the card file allowing lookup of cards by account number
files.CXACAIX: Card cross-reference alternate index file used to resolve an account number to its associated card and customer records

business_rules: The account number entered must be exactly 11 digits, numeric, and non-zero; otherwise an error message is displayed and the staff member is prompted to re-enter.
The account number must exist in the card cross-reference file (CXACAIX); if not found, the staff member is informed that the account cannot be located.
The account must exist in the account master file (ACCTDAT); if not found, an appropriate error is displayed.
The customer associated with the account must exist in the customer master file (CUSTDAT); if not found, an error is displayed indicating the customer record is missing.
Only the Enter key and PF3 (exit/back) are treated as valid keystrokes; any other function key press is ignored and treated as Enter.
Pressing PF3 returns the staff member to the previously calling program/transaction (or the main menu if no prior context exists), ensuring consistent navigation within the application.
The program is a read-only view; no account or customer data is modified by this program — updates are delegated to COACTUPC and card updates to COCRDUPC.
From the account view screen, staff can navigate to the card list (COCRDLIC) or card detail/update (COCRDSLC/COCRDUPC) screens for further action on the account's cards.

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage group that holds all temporary variables used during the account viewing process, including processing flags, input validation results, file lookup keys, and messages displayed to bank staff.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to track the outcome of CICS system calls made during account and customer data retrieval, helping the program detect and respond to technical errors from the mainframe transaction environment.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The primary response code returned by CICS after each file read or system operation. A non-zero value indicates that something went wrong when trying to retrieve account, customer, or card data — for example, a record not found or a file unavailable.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The secondary reason code returned by CICS alongside the primary response code, providing additional detail about why a file operation failed — for example, distinguishing between a record not found versus a file I/O error during account lookup.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The 4-character CICS transaction identifier for the current account view screen session. Used to identify which transaction is running so the program can manage screen navigation and return routing correctly.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall status flag indicating whether the account number entered by the bank staff member is ready to be processed. Drives the program's decision to proceed with the account lookup or re-display the screen with an error.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member has passed all validation checks and the program can proceed to retrieve account and customer details.

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member failed validation — for example, it was blank, non-numeric, or zero — and the screen must be re-displayed with an appropriate error message.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that no input has yet been received from the staff member — the screen has just been displayed for the first time and is awaiting an account number entry.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Flag that records whether the function key pressed by the bank staff member is one the program recognises and supports. Only Enter and PF3 are valid; all other keys set this flag to invalid.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member pressed a recognised and supported function key (Enter or PF3), so the program can proceed with the intended action such as looking up an account or navigating back.

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member pressed an unsupported function key. The program will ignore the key and treat the action as if Enter was pressed, preventing unintended navigation or errors.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that no function key input has yet been captured — the screen is in its initial state before the staff member has interacted with it.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ACCT-FLAG
variables.description: Indicates whether the account number entered by the staff member passed all business validation rules (11 digits, numeric, non-zero). Controls whether the program proceeds to look up the account in the master file or stops and prompts for correction.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member failed validation — it may be non-numeric, zero, or the wrong length — and cannot be used to search for an account.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member is valid (11 digits, numeric, non-zero) and the program can proceed to look up the account in the card cross-reference and account master files.

variables.name: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number field has not yet been evaluated — the validation check has not been performed, typically because the screen has just been displayed for the first time.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CUST-FLAG
variables.description: Indicates whether a valid customer record was found in the customer master file (CUSTDAT) for the account being viewed. If no customer is found, the program displays an error to the staff member rather than showing incomplete account details.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer associated with the account could not be found in the customer master file, meaning the account view cannot be completed and an error must be shown to the staff member.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer record was successfully retrieved from the customer master file and the full account and customer details can be displayed to the staff member.

variables.name: FLG-CUSTFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer lookup has not yet been attempted — the flag is in its initial uninitialised state, typically before the account number has been validated and submitted.

variables.name: WS-XREF-RID
variables.description: Group of record identifier fields used as lookup keys when searching the card cross-reference file (CXACAIX). Together these fields allow the program to resolve a card number to its associated account and customer records.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number used as the primary key to look up the card cross-reference record, which links the card to its associated account and customer. This is the starting point for resolving an account number to full account and customer details.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID
variables.description: The 9-digit customer identifier retrieved from the card cross-reference file, used to look up the customer's personal and contact details in the customer master file (CUSTDAT) for display on the account view screen.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X
variables.description: Alphanumeric alias for the customer identifier field, allowing the 9-digit customer ID to be treated as a character string when needed — for example, during display formatting or character-level validation.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The 11-digit account identifier used to retrieve the account master record from ACCTDAT. This is the key account reference that the staff member enters on screen, and it drives the entire account lookup process.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X
variables.description: Alphanumeric alias for the account identifier field, allowing the 11-digit account ID to be treated as a character string — for example, when validating that the entered value is numeric or when formatting it for display.

variables.name: WS-FILE-READ-FLAGS
variables.description: Group of flags that record whether the account and customer master records were successfully retrieved from their respective files. These flags control whether the program can display complete account details or must show an error to the staff member.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-MASTER-READ-FLAG
variables.description: Indicates whether the account record was successfully read from the account master file (ACCTDAT). If the account was not found, the program cannot display account details such as credit limit, balance, or status.

variables.name: FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account record was successfully retrieved from the account master file (ACCTDAT), meaning the program can display the account's credit limit, balance, status, and other details to the staff member.

variables.name: WS-CUST-MASTER-READ-FLAG
variables.description: Indicates whether the customer record was successfully read from the customer master file (CUSTDAT). If the customer was not found, the program cannot display the account holder's personal and contact details.

variables.name: FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer record was successfully retrieved from the customer master file (CUSTDAT), meaning the program can display the account holder's name, address, and contact information alongside the account details.

variables.name: WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: A structured error message template that is assembled and displayed (or logged) when a file read operation fails. It captures the operation attempted, the file involved, and the CICS response codes, helping support staff diagnose technical problems during account lookup.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Fixed label text at the start of the file error message — for example, a prefix such as 'ERROR ON  ' — providing context that this is a file operation error message.

variables.name: ERROR-OPNAME
variables.description: The name of the file operation that failed — for example, 'READ    ' — helping support staff understand what action was being performed when the error occurred during account or customer data retrieval.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Separator or label text between the operation name and the file name in the error message — for example, ' ON ' — improving readability of the error message displayed to support staff.

variables.name: ERROR-FILE
variables.description: The name of the file that could not be read — for example, 'ACCTDAT  ' or 'CUSTDAT  ' — identifying which data source caused the failure so support staff can investigate the correct file or dataset.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Separator or label text between the file name and the response code in the error message — for example, ' RESP CODE:    ' — making the error message easier to read for support staff.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP
variables.description: The primary CICS response code from the failed file operation, formatted as text for display. This code helps technical support staff identify the category of error — for example, record not found or file unavailable — when diagnosing account lookup failures.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Separator or label text between the primary and secondary response codes in the error message — for example, ' RESP2: ' — maintaining a readable format for the error details shown to support staff.

variables.name: ERROR-RESP2
variables.description: The secondary CICS reason code from the failed file operation, formatted as text for display. This provides additional detail beyond the primary response code to help support staff pinpoint the exact cause of the file read failure during account lookup.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Trailing padding at the end of the file error message, ensuring the message field is fully populated and correctly aligned when displayed or written to a log.

variables.name: WS-LONG-MSG
variables.description: A large text buffer used to hold extended diagnostic or informational messages during account lookup processing — for example, detailed error descriptions that may be written to a log or used internally for debugging when a file operation fails.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: A short informational prompt displayed at the top or bottom of the account view screen to guide the bank staff member — for example, instructing them to enter an account number or confirming that account details are being displayed.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that there is no informational prompt to display to the staff member — the info message area on the screen is blank, typically when the screen is in a neutral state.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the staff member to enter an account number — displayed when the screen first loads or after an error has been cleared and the staff member needs to try again.

variables.name: WS-INFORM-OUTPUT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is displaying a result message to the staff member — for example, confirming that account details have been successfully retrieved and are now shown on screen.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: The main status or error message displayed to the bank staff member at the bottom of the account view screen, explaining the outcome of the last action — such as a validation failure, a record not found, or a successful account retrieval.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that there is no return message to display — the message area is blank, typically when the screen is in a clean state with no errors or status updates to communicate to the staff member.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is informing the staff member that they are exiting the account view screen — displayed when PF3 is pressed and the program is navigating back to the calling screen or main menu.

variables.name: WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the return message is prompting the staff member to enter a valid account number — displayed when the screen first loads or when a previous entry was invalid and needs to be corrected.

variables.name: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member submitted the screen without entering any account number — the return message informs them that an account number is required to perform a lookup.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-ZEROES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the staff member entered all zeros as the account number — the return message informs them that this is not a valid account number and they must enter a real account identifier.

variables.name: SEARCHED-ACCT-NOT-NUMERIC
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member contains non-numeric characters — the return message informs them that the account number must consist of digits only.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF
variables.description: Condition indicating that the account number entered by the staff member could not be found in the card cross-reference file (CXACAIX) — the return message informs them that no card or account record exists for that number.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT
variables.description: Condition indicating that although the account number was found in the card cross-reference, no matching record exists in the account master file (ACCTDAT) — the return message informs the staff member that the account details cannot be retrieved.

variables.name: DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT
variables.description: Condition indicating that the customer associated with the account could not be found in the customer master file (CUSTDAT) — the return message informs the staff member that the account holder's personal details are missing from the system.

variables.name: XREF-READ-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that a technical error occurred while reading the card cross-reference file (CXACAIX) — the return message informs the staff member that the lookup failed due to a system error rather than a missing record.

variables.name: CODING-TO-BE-DONE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the program has reached a processing path that has not yet been fully implemented — a placeholder message displayed to the staff member or developer indicating that this functionality is pending development.

variables.name: WS-LITERALS
variables.description: Top-level group containing constant text values and fixed literals used throughout the account view program — for example, standard screen messages, labels, and fixed strings that do not change during processing.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The hardcoded name of this account view program (COACTVWC). Used internally to identify the current program when setting up navigation context or passing control to other screens.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS transaction ID associated with this account view screen. Used to re-invoke this screen correctly when returning from a sub-screen or refreshing the display.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS mapset name for the account view screen layout. Identifies the collection of screen maps (COACTVW) that define how account information is displayed to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS map name for the specific account view screen. Identifies the exact screen layout used to display account and customer details to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTPGM
variables.description: The hardcoded program name for the credit card list screen (COCRDLIC). Used when bank staff navigate from the account view to see all credit cards associated with the account.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTTRANID
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS transaction ID for the credit card list screen. Used to launch the card listing transaction when bank staff want to view all cards linked to the account being viewed.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAPSET
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS mapset name for the credit card list screen. Identifies the screen layout collection used when displaying the list of cards associated with an account.

variables.name: LIT-CCLISTMAP
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS map name for the credit card list screen. Identifies the specific screen layout used to present the list of credit cards linked to the account being viewed.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATEPGM
variables.description: The hardcoded program name for the credit card update screen (COCRDUPC). Used when bank staff need to navigate from the account view to modify details of a specific credit card linked to the account.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUDPATETRANID
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS transaction ID for the credit card update screen. Used to launch the card update transaction when bank staff want to modify a card record associated with the account being viewed.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATEMAPSET
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS mapset name for the credit card update screen. Identifies the screen layout collection used when bank staff update credit card details from within the account view workflow.

variables.name: LIT-CARDUPDATEMAP
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS map name for the credit card update screen. Identifies the specific screen layout presented to bank staff when editing a credit card record linked to the account.

variables.name: LIT-MENUPGM
variables.description: The hardcoded program name for the main menu of the CardDemo application. Used as the fallback navigation destination when bank staff press PF3 to exit and there is no prior calling program to return to.

variables.name: LIT-MENUTRANID
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS transaction ID for the main menu screen. Used to return bank staff to the application's main menu when pressing PF3 without a prior navigation context.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAPSET
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS mapset name for the main menu screen. Identifies the screen layout collection for the application's main menu, used during back-navigation when no prior screen context exists.

variables.name: LIT-MENUMAP
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS map name for the main menu screen. Identifies the specific main menu layout displayed to bank staff when they exit the account view with no prior screen to return to.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLPGM
variables.description: The hardcoded program name for the credit card detail/selection screen (COCRDSLC). Used when bank staff navigate from the account view to inspect the full details of a specific credit card.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLTRANID
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS transaction ID for the credit card detail screen. Used to launch the card detail transaction when bank staff select a specific card for closer inspection from the account view.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAPSET
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS mapset name for the credit card detail screen. Identifies the screen layout collection used when displaying full details of a single credit card to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-CARDDTLMAP
variables.description: The hardcoded BMS map name for the credit card detail screen. Identifies the specific screen layout used to present all details of a selected credit card to bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-ACCTFILENAME
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS file name for the account master file (ACCTDAT). Used when the program reads account details such as credit limit, balance, and status for the account number entered by bank staff.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS file name for the card master file (CARDDAT). Used when the program retrieves individual credit card records linked to the account being viewed.

variables.name: LIT-CUSTFILENAME
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS file name for the customer master file (CUSTDAT). Used when the program retrieves the personal and contact details of the customer associated with the account being viewed.

variables.name: LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS file name for the alternate index on the card file (CARDAIX) that allows lookup by account number. Used to find all credit cards belonging to a given account when only the account number is known.

variables.name: LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH
variables.description: The hardcoded CICS file name for the card cross-reference alternate index (CXACAIX). Used to resolve an account number entered by bank staff into the associated card number and customer ID needed to retrieve full account and customer records.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM
variables.description: A hardcoded reference string containing all 52 alphabetic characters (both uppercase and lowercase). Used as the source string in character translation operations, such as converting lowercase input from bank staff to uppercase for consistent data processing.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A hardcoded string of 52 space characters used as the target in character translation operations. Paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM to strip or blank out alphabetic characters during input validation, ensuring account number fields contain only numeric digits.

variables.name: LIT-UPPER
variables.description: A hardcoded string of all 26 uppercase letters (A–Z). Used in character translation to convert any lowercase input entered by bank staff into uppercase, ensuring consistent formatting of text fields.

variables.name: LIT-LOWER
variables.description: A hardcoded string of all 26 lowercase letters (a–z). Used alongside LIT-UPPER in character translation to identify and convert lowercase characters entered by bank staff into their uppercase equivalents.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: A working-storage communication area specific to this account view program. Holds the identity of the screen or program that called this account view, enabling correct back-navigation when bank staff press PF3 to exit.

variables.name: CA-CALL-CONTEXT
variables.description: Groups the navigation context fields that identify where bank staff came from before arriving at the account view screen, supporting the PF3 back-navigation business rule.

variables.name: CA-FROM-PROGRAM
variables.description: The name of the program that navigated bank staff to this account view screen. When staff press PF3 to go back, this value determines which program to return to, ensuring seamless navigation within the CardDemo application.

variables.name: CA-FROM-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID of the screen that sent bank staff to this account view. Used alongside CA-FROM-PROGRAM to correctly re-invoke the prior screen when staff press PF3 to exit the account view.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: A general-purpose working-storage buffer used to hold the full CICS communication area data passed between programs. Acts as a staging area for reading and writing the shared application context (such as account, customer, and navigation information) when transferring control between CardDemo screens.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area received by this program when it is invoked. Contains data passed from the previously executing program, including account context, user identity, and navigation state, allowing the account view screen to know what account to display and where to return when the staff member exits.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: An unnamed placeholder within the DFHCOMMAREA definition. Ensures the communication area structure is correctly aligned in memory; has no direct business meaning but is required for the program to correctly interpret the data passed from the calling program.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration paragraph that controls the entire account view session: it initialises the screen environment, determines what the staff member pressed, and routes the transaction to the correct action — whether that is displaying the account lookup screen, processing a submitted account number, or navigating back to the calling menu.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph finalises the current screen interaction and returns control to the Account View transaction, preserving any result or error message for the staff member and carrying forward the full application session context so the next screen interaction can resume seamlessly.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine, signalling that all account viewing operations for the current interaction have completed and control is returned to the calling environment.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the main processing routine, signalling that all account viewing operations for the current interaction have completed and control is returned to the calling environment.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full preparation and delivery of the Account View screen to the bank staff member, coordinating screen initialisation, data population, field formatting, and final display in a single logical sequence.

paragraphs.name: 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that displays account and customer details to the bank staff member. It acts as a structural boundary ensuring the display logic terminates cleanly before control returns to the calling section.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises the Account View screen before displaying it to the bank staff member, clearing any previous data and populating the screen header with the application titles, current transaction and program identifiers, and the current date and time.

paragraphs.name: 1100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point marking the end of the screen initialisation routine. It contains no business logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary that signals the completion of the screen setup process.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares all data fields on the Account View screen for display, populating account financial details and customer personal information retrieved from the master files. It also sets the appropriate guidance and status messages to inform the bank staff member of the outcome of their lookup request.

paragraphs.name: 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen variable setup routine, marking the end of the process that prepares account and customer details for display on the Account View screen.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph configures the visual presentation of the Account View screen before it is displayed to the staff member, setting field protection, cursor position, and colour coding to guide the user based on the current validation state of the account number they entered.

paragraphs.name: 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen attribute setup routine, marking the end of the process that configures how account and customer information is visually presented to the bank staff member. It contains no logic of its own and simply signals the completion of the calling setup process.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the Account View screen to the bank staff member's terminal, displaying the current account and customer details (or any validation/error messages) and returning control to the staff member for further input or navigation.

paragraphs.name: 1400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen-sending routine, marking the end of the process that displays the account view screen to the bank staff member. It is a structural boundary used by the program to cleanly conclude the screen presentation logic.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the processing of staff input from the Account View screen: it collects what the staff member entered, validates the account number, and prepares the screen to redisplay with the appropriate result message and navigation context.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input processing routine, allowing the program to cleanly conclude the validation and data retrieval phase before proceeding to display account information on screen.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the account number entered by the bank staff member from the Account View screen, reading all input fields submitted by the user into the program for subsequent validation and processing.

paragraphs.name: 2100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the map-receiving routine, marking the end of the process that captures the account number entered by the staff member from the screen. It contains no logic itself, acting purely as a structural boundary that allows other parts of the program to branch here cleanly when the screen input capture step is complete.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number entered by the bank staff member on the Account View screen, ensuring it is present and properly formatted before any file lookups are attempted. It prepares the input for downstream validation and flags the search as incomplete if no account number was provided.

paragraphs.name: 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account number validation routine, marking the end of all input checks before the program proceeds to retrieve account and customer data. It acts as a structured boundary ensuring the validation logic completes cleanly before any file lookups are attempted.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates the account number entered by the bank staff member before any file lookups are attempted. It ensures the account number is present, numeric, non-zero, and exactly 11 digits, rejecting invalid input with an appropriate message.

paragraphs.name: 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the account number validation routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling section after all validation checks on the entered account number have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-ACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full account lookup process by sequentially retrieving the card cross-reference, account master, and customer master records for a given account number. It acts as the central coordinator ensuring all three data sources are successfully resolved before the account details can be displayed to the bank staff member.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account retrieval routine, allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling logic after the account lookup process has completed, whether successfully or with an error.

paragraphs.name: 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph looks up the card cross-reference file using the account number entered by the staff member to retrieve the associated customer identifier and credit card number. It is the critical linking step that resolves an account number into the customer and card details needed to display the full account view.

paragraphs.name: 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the card cross-reference lookup routine. It marks the end of the account-to-card cross-reference retrieval process, allowing control to return cleanly to the calling logic after the lookup has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the full account record from the account master file using the account number identified during the cross-reference lookup. It handles three outcomes: a successful retrieval, an account not found, or an unexpected system error — setting appropriate status flags and staff-facing messages accordingly.

paragraphs.name: 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the account data retrieval routine, marking the end of the process that looks up and loads the full account record from the account master file. It ensures a clean, structured return to the calling logic after account retrieval has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the personal and contact details of the customer associated with a credit card account from the customer master file. It handles all possible outcomes — successful retrieval, customer not found, or an unexpected system error — and sets appropriate status flags and error messages for display to the bank staff member.

paragraphs.name: 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the customer data retrieval routine, marking the end of the process that looks up a customer's personal details by their customer identifier. It contains no business logic and simply signals the completion of the customer lookup step, returning control to the calling part of the program.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the display of a plain-text result or error message to the bank staff member's screen and then terminates the current transaction, returning control to CICS. It is used when the program needs to communicate a simple outcome — such as a validation failure or lookup error — without rendering the full account view screen.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a no-operation exit point for a diagnostic text display routine, intended only for debugging purposes and not part of the normal account viewing workflow. It acts as a placeholder that immediately exits without performing any business action.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph displays a full-screen plain-text message to the bank staff member — typically used for error or diagnostic information that is too long for a standard screen field — and then terminates the current transaction, returning control to CICS.

paragraphs.name: SEND-LONG-TEXT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the screen text transmission routine, marking the end of that process. It also incorporates shared logic for capturing and storing which function key the staff member pressed, enabling correct navigation handling.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable system failures in the Account View program by capturing diagnostic information, notifying the system of the failure, and terminating the session in a controlled manner. It ensures that when a critical error occurs, a meaningful error record is preserved and the transaction is cleanly abended rather than left in an unknown state.
